title: Project Requirements, Design, Test, and Review
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of project requirements, design, test, and review.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: Project workflow begins by understanding the problem and defining requirements. Design describes data, responsibilities, and interactions before implementation. Testing checks behavior against criteria; review considers quality, maintainability, security, and usability. These activities are iterative: discoveries during implementation can update the plan, but changes should be tracked and justified.
understand.whyItMatters: A repeatable workflow reduces confusion and makes project decisions and quality checks visible.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
Project workflow begins by understanding the problem and defining requirements. Design describes data, responsibilities, and interactions before implementation. Testing checks behavior against criteria; review considers quality, maintainability, security, and usability. These activities are iterative: discoveries during implementation can update the plan, but changes should be tracked and justified.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Use a one-page template to plan a tiny project: problem, users, requirements, non-goals, data model, functions, risks, test cases, and review notes. Then implement one requirement and test it.
steps: Use a one-page template to plan a tiny project: problem, users, requirements, non-goals, data model, functions, risks, test cases, and review notes. Then implement one requirement and test it.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: For a project of your choice, complete a requirements/design/test/review cycle. Keep evidence for requirements, design decisions, tests, issues found, fixes, and final status. Explain one trade-off.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
